advisories.name: PHP2Shell
advisories.title: Your PHP has the 'PHP2Shell' break-in flaw
advisories.summary: Two critical flaws in PHP itself (the software your website runs on) let a stranger take over the website with a single web request - no password needed. Attacks started on October 21, 2026. Updating WordPress or plugins does NOT fix this; only updating PHP does.
advisories.fix: Update PHP to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, 8.5.12 or newer. On regular web hosting your hosting company controls this - send them the ready-made message below. If you run your own server, update the PHP packages and restart PHP-FPM / your web server.
advisories.support_ask: Please confirm my website's PHP has the fix for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (PHP2Shell): PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, 8.5.12 or newer, or a security backport.
advisories.backport_note: Some Linux distributions fix this without changing the version number. If your host says the fix is 'backported', you are fine - mark this as resolved.
